$comment: MCP tool contract for `diverge`. inputSchema/outputSchema are what the server advertises in its tool catalog. k stance-blind passes under distinct generative lenses; the server deduplicates deterministically and labels each framing with its lens. BASELINE, captured from the derived schemas at 038 rather than authored ahead of the code - this tool shipped without a contract, so there is no earlier statement of intent to restore. Its value starts now: any change to the Rust types fails the contract test until this file is updated deliberately. Neither `problem` nor `context` carries a `maxLength`: the size bound is `INPUT_MAX_CHARS`, a deployment setting, and a schema cannot state a number the operator chooses. It applies to the two fields **combined**, since both reach the prompt (052; before it, `context` was not bounded at all, so a request with a large context that this server previously accepted is now rejected).
name: diverge

inputSchema.description: Tool input: the problem the caller is anchored on, plus optional neutral context.

context.description:
Optional neutral context a pass may consult — the only extra information a
pass receives. There is no slot for the caller's stance or preferred answer.

anyOf.description:
How much reasoning a call site should spend (022).

Maps to the provider's `output_config.effort`. It governs *all* output
tokens, thinking included, and is a behavioural signal rather than a hard
token budget — `MAX_TOKENS` remains the ceiling.

Unset is not `High`: an unset call site sends no `effort` field at all, so
the request body is byte-identical to before this feature. The provider's
own default is `high`, so unset and `High` behave the same, but only unset
is provably unchanged on the wire.

oneOf.description: Minimal reasoning; thinking skipped on simple tasks.
Moderate reasoning; thinking may be skipped on simple queries.
Deep reasoning on complex tasks. The provider's default.
Always thinks, no constraint on depth.
Always thinks deeply, with extended exploration.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for this call alone. Omit to use the deployment's
configured level. Not every model family accepts this; when one rejects
it the error names the model, the level, and the remedies.

Typed rather than a free string so the accepted levels appear in the
published schema — the consumer of this server is a model reading that
schema, and a prose-only list is not something it can be constrained by.

passes.description:
Independent passes to run for this call alone. **Minimum 1.** The
effective maximum is the deployment's configured count, not a fixed
number, so it cannot appear in the schema — a request above it is
rejected with an error naming the ceiling.

May be **lower** than the configured count, never higher: each pass is
a whole model call, so raising it would buy work the operator did not
authorise. Omit to use the configured count. Each pass applies a distinct
generative lens, so fewer passes means fewer distinct framings; the
result reports the count it actually used.

problem.description: The framing the caller is anchored on, stated neutrally.

inputSchema.title: DivergeParams

Perspective.description:
One returned framing — a [`DivergePass`] labeled with the lens that produced
it (server-assembled).

outputSchema.description:
The aggregated tool output (data-model.md) — the deduplicated set of distinct
framings. No verdict, no confidence: `diverge` scatters, it does not converge.

perspectives.description: The deduplicated perspectives, in pass order (≤ k distinct).

outputSchema.title: DivergeResult
